acceptedAnswer.text: The Pair is a free, open-source AI pair programming desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. It runs two AI coding agents, a read-only Mentor and an Executor, so coding work is planned, implemented, tested, and reviewed by separate roles.

mainEntity.name: How is The Pair different from Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or Aider?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Aider usually rely on one assistant to write code and self-review. The Pair is a Cursor and Copilot alternative that separates responsibilities: the Mentor reviews while the Executor changes code and runs verification.

mainEntity.name: Which AI providers does The Pair support?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Pair supports opencode, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and Kimi Code CLI. Developers can mix providers between Mentor and Executor, including local models through Ollama-compatible opencode routes.
Yes. The Pair orchestrates agents locally in a native Tauri desktop app. Only selected model providers need network access unless the developer uses a local model provider.

mainEntity.name: How does The Pair reduce AI coding hallucinations?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Pair reduces AI coding hallucinations by splitting the workflow into two roles. The Executor writes and verifies code, while the read-only Mentor reviews the result, requests fixes, and prevents unreviewed changes from being accepted too early.
